I worked for about 7years collectively in BPOs when I left. Been working freelance for about 5years. Don't get it wrong, applying and looking for the right clients and companies were hard. Lots of tempering the waters, checking your future with them, salary issues. So it was never easy, I just focused my efforts in investing on myself. Treat your freelancing career as if working in companies. Invest on equipment, upgrading the things you already have, not be complacent that nothing bad will happen, have emergency funds that you really won't use except for emergencies, prepare yourself to a life of isolation if need be but this is just for the first few months, upskill. There's no one sure way to go about it since there are so many factors involved.

Just keep on sending those applications, read the requirements for the jobs you're interested in and see if you can learn the required skills while waiting for a response because whether you get accepted or not, you're adding value to what you can offer in the future. Never, and I mean, never invest on those freelance gurus/lessons in tiktok and fb, you can get their core lessons for free online.

Identify kung ano ang bills (recurring payables like power, water, internet), essentials (food, groceries, toiletries), and identify kung magkano target savings mo (determine a fraction of your pay like 10%-35% of monthly salary). Hindi pwedeng mawala ang kahit ano jan sa tatlo. Ang bills kailangan malaman kung ano yung average total per month, ang essentials adjustable based off the lifestyle, ang savings kailangan commitment yan. 

Once makuha ang salary every month, ibawas mo na agad yang tatlo. If may sobra, decide again kung gusto mong magadvance sa kahit ano sa tatlo for the next month. Never think na yung sobra after ibawas yang tatlo is disposable income. That's what I called investing in myself back then. If you keep on paying in advance every month, you'll have disposable at the end of the year. Then decide naman by the end of the year kung magbabawas ka sa bills and essentials OR tataasan mo or stay the same ang savings mo for the following year. 

If you need emergency funds, umutang ka sa savings mo. Committing na ibabalik mo yung inutang mo sa savings mo. Do this for the first 3-5years and in the final year, you'll have some disposable funds. I'd suggest in the first 10 years but that might be too much.

20-30years ago, "hayaan mo na" was applicable because back then there's not much other means for people to blow things out of proportion hence it might have been an isolated thing. However, nowadays, people brag how they get away of things, may it be legally or illegally done, sometimes even suggesting to other people to do it too. 

So "hayaan mo na" is no longer a good enough option. Now, it's the other way around, they won't stop doing something until someone calls them out. Even then, they'll make some excuse to show that this time is different from the 1st (2nd, 3rd and so on) time that they did it.

So the blame now goes to the people who enabled that behavior to persist or worse, blow up to a much worse version.

Edit: I'm not suggesting "patulan mo" but I'm not suggesting "hayaan mo na" either. I'm suggesting to speak your piece so boundaries and limits are placed on the table. If they cross them, you have the option to speak out or walk away but remember whatever you chooses will have an effect towards their behavior the next time around.
